episode_title: Mastering Agentic AI: An Interview with Martin Kihn, Senior Vice President, Strategy at Salesforce

real_qa.q: What is the biggest mindset shift companies need to make to successfully deploy AI according to Salesforce's Agent Force observations?
real_qa.r: Companies need to see AI as a tool, not a cure-all solution. It requires education, implementation, and actually more work than people think. Approach it the way you would any new technology, focusing on incremental improvements rather than expecting magic transformations. The key is realistic expectations about what AI can do rather than fear-based thinking.

real_qa.q: Why do most AI pilot projects fail to scale in marketing organizations?
real_qa.r: Marketers are plugging AI into current ways of doing things instead of rethinking processes from scratch. They want to keep doing what they've always done, only faster, rather than using AI to reimagine the customer experience. Additionally, legacy systems and stove-piped tools cannot handle the demands of generative AI, and dirty data in disconnected systems prevents hyper-personalization from working effectively.
real_qa.requete: why AI marketing pilots fail scale

real_qa.q: How is Salesforce Agent Force being used differently in customer service compared to initial expectations?
real_qa.r: Instead of replacing human workers entirely, companies are adding agents to their teams as a hybrid workforce. Humans continue their existing work while agents handle tasks that previously couldn't get done due to insufficient staffing. Leads that were scored and ignored in the past now get handled by agents, and customers like ReMarkable use Net Promoter Score to measure both agents and humans on the same team.
real_qa.requete: Agent Force customer service hybrid human agents

real_qa.q: How does AI's impact on marketing fundamentally differ from its disruption of customer service and sales roles?
real_qa.r: Marketing is more complicated than customer service and B2B sales because it is campaign-related and addresses a much greater number of people. Customer service is highly predictable (80% of retailer calls are either order tracking or returns), while marketing requires multiple interdependent agents that must work together: creating campaigns, identifying audiences, developing creative, and planning media—making automation much slower to implement.
real_qa.requete: AI marketing disruption vs customer service sales

real_qa.q: What unified data foundation do AI agents require to operate effectively in marketing?
real_qa.r: AI agents require access to unstructured data like call center logs, website content, videos, and text. Customer data platforms have evolved into vector databases that can load unstructured content and make it accessible to agents. A unified, real-time customer profile that is properly documented is essential, making customer data platforms more important than ever when deploying agentic AI.
real_qa.requete: AI agents data foundation customer data platform

guest.titre: Senior Vice President, Strategy for Marketing Cloud
guest.bio_context: Martin Kihn is the Senior Vice President of Strategy for Salesforce's Marketing Cloud and author of three books on enterprise technology: Customer Data Platforms, Customer 360 (co-authored), and Agent Force. He previously worked in advertising agencies including Digitas and Fallon during the formative years of the Internet in the 1990s and early 2000s. His expertise lies in translating complex technical concepts into plain language that marketers can understand.
